findings.page: PDF p. 149 (printed p. 125); related PDF p. 89 (printed 65), Ch. 4
findings.evidence: Rendered image of PDF p. 149 shows the in-figure axis label on the vertical SLO line: "SLO 2 s (TTFT budget)". The figure's own caption on the same page reads: "the p95 TTFT ceiling (Ch 4, Table 4-1 Latency row; Canonical Workload box), not the 1.2 s design budget — a superset of TTFT violations". Ch. 4, Table 4-1 Latency row (PDF p. 89) defines: "TTFT budget 1.2 s (retrieval ~120 ms + prefill ~1.08 s); TPOT budget ~25 ms/token; p95 TTFT ≤ 2 s, p95 TPOT ≤ 35 ms".
findings.issue: The figure's own axis label calls the 2 s value the "TTFT budget", which is the opposite of the book's definition and of the caption printed directly beneath it: 1.2 s is the design budget, ≤ 2 s is the p95 ceiling. The book treats this pair as load-bearing ("Where a distinction is load-bearing ... the book holds it sharply: synonyms are a readability concession, and load-bearing contrasts are never relaxed", Preface, PDF p. 22). A reader who copies the axis label into a dashboard, an SLO slide or an ADR will record the wrong budget; only the caption corrects it, and a caption is read less often than an axis label.
findings.fix_instruction: Re-render Fig. 6.2 with the in-figure label changed to "SLO 2 s (p95 TTFT ceiling)" (and, if the design budget is also plotted, label it "1.2 s TTFT design budget"). Grep the whole figure set for the string "TTFT budget" applied to the 2 s line and apply the same fix anywhere it appears (any figure reusing the 2 s line).
